datasheet.title: 7280R3 Series Data Center Switch Router Data Sheet (Arista Networks, 03-0045-59, August 11th, 2025)

description: Arista 7280SR3-40YC6 - a fixed 1RU data-centre switch router with 40 x 1/10/25G SFP ports and 6 x 100G QSFP ports, running EOS. The front carries the SFP cages in two stacked rows of twenty columns in two-column blocks, the odd number on top, with a status lamp at each end of every block row, and the six QSFP cages in two stacked rows of three columns at the right. Four system lamps (system, fan, PS1, PS2) are in a column at the far right. The rear carries two hot-swap 500 W power supplies at the ends and two hot-swap fan modules, with the RJ-45 management port, the USB port and the RJ-45 console port between the left supply and the first fan. The same panel is ordered with front-to-rear air (-F) or rear-to-front air (-R). It is sold as the 7280SR3-40YC6 and, with SyncE and more memory, as the 7280SR3E-40YC6-M.

gaps.note: Weight of the 7280SR3-40YC6: 10.7 kg (guide Table 1) against 9.57 kg (data sheet, which gives the plain and E-M models the same cell). The guide gives the 7280SR3E-40YC6-M 9.6 kg and the 7280TR3-40C6 9.6 kg for the same hardware class, so the 10.7 is taken as the outlier; the data sheet's is used.
gaps.wanted: the maker's statement of which is current.

gaps.note: Storage temperature -25 to 70 C (guide Table 2) against -40 to 70 C (data sheet), and relative humidity 5 to 90 percent against 5 to 95 percent. The guide's, the older document by three months, are in attrs.
gaps.wanted: the maker's statement of which is current.

gaps.note: The 7280SR3E-40YC6-M has 32 GB of memory against 8 GB, inband SyncE, and (guide Table 4) the same power draw. No configuration can state a device attribute (the same open gap as cisco/asr-9001). The platform lines name both.

The guide's Figures 3-1 to 3-4 are isometric drawings of another switch and carry no measure, and the kit guides for KIT-7101 and the other spares are not held, so no ear position or rail kit is written.
gaps.wanted: a dimensioned drawing of the mounting bracket position, and the kit guides.

gaps.note: Figure C-7 draws a column of three or four green dots at the left edge of each QSFP cage. Their count and meaning are not resolved at 125 ppi, so no QSFP lamp is modelled; the SFP lamps are.
gaps.wanted: a photograph of the lit face.

gaps.note: The small numbers with triangles above the cages, the small print on the strips, the system and fan lamp glyphs and the model line are barely readable in the 847 px figure. The lamp glyphs and the PS1 and PS2 legends are drawn as read; the strip and cage legends are not drawn, and the numbers are printed in the band between the rows.
Which side the latches of the stacked cages face is not visible in the figure. The library's belly-to-belly convention is used (upper cage upright, lower turned 180).
gaps.wanted: a photograph of the stacked cages.

gaps.note: The management block's arrow marks and its console symbol are drawn as the 7280CR3-32D4 draws them; the order of the three ports follows the datasheet's rear view and the library's other Arista stacks, and the figure's 1.25 px/mm resolves it only as three stacked ports.
gaps.wanted: a photograph of the rear management block.

gaps.note: The PWR-511-DC supplies are drawn as the AC supply's housing with a plain two-pole terminal block. The guide shows a DC supply only in isometric figures; the real terminal arrangement is not drawn.
gaps.wanted: a flat drawing or photograph of the PWR-511-DC.

gaps.note: The guide's power tables and the data sheet give whole-switch figures only; the fan modules' missing power figure (lint L27) stands. The supplies state their output.
The 1RU grounding point is on the bottom of the chassis for KIT-GND-EXT-1RU (guide section 4.2, Table 5, Figure 4-2). No flat figure measures it, so it is not placed.
gaps.wanted: a flat drawing of the bottom with the grounding bracket holes.

port-leds.description: a status lamp for each SFP port, at the outer edge of its block

psu-bays.description: the two hot-swap power supplies, 1+1 redundant

status-leds.description: the system, fan and two power supply lamps at the far right of the front

name: 7280sr3-40yc6

chassis.note: Guide Table 1: 48.3 x 4.4 x 46.9 cm (19 x 1.75 x 18.5 in), 10.7 kg (23.6 lbs) for the 7280SR3-40YC6 and 9.6 kg (21.0 lbs) for the 7280SR3E-40YC6-M. Data sheet: 43.99 x 4.37 x 46.9 cm (17.3 x 1.72 x 18.46 in), 21.1 lbs (9.57 kg) for both. The width: 48.3 cm is over the mounting ears, so the body between them, which is what is modelled, is the data sheet's 43.99 cm (440.0 here), a 21.5 mm ear each side. The height is the data sheet's 43.7. The depth is the data sheet's 469.0 (the guide's 46.9 cm). The weight conflicts (the guide's 10.7 kg for the plain model is the outlier against its own 9.6 kg for the same-hardware E-M and the data sheet's 9.57 kg; gap `size-conflict`); the data sheet's is in attrs. 1RU.

colour.note: The front plate is the 7280CR3-32D4's #aaabad, read there as the median of bare-plate pixels in the guide's figure of the same family.

configurations.note: Data sheet ordering information: DCS-7280SR3-40YC6-F and -R, and DCS-7280SR3E-40YC6-M-F and -R ("SyncE, expn. mem, front to rear air, 2 x AC" and "rear to front air, 2 x AC"). The guide's Figure C-7 is captioned for both models, so the E-M build has the same face and is a configuration with its own part numbers. The "#" SKUs ("configurable fans and psu") are orders of parts, not part numbers a DCIM can hold, and are not listed. The data sheet lists no DC build of the switch: the PWR-511-DC-RED and -BLUE supplies are spares, so the DC configurations are examples with no part number. There is no empty-bay (-S) configuration: no -S suffix exists in this family and the guide draws no blank for a power supply or fan module. The 7280TR3-40C6, which shares this guide table and the data sheet ordering page, has no front figure in the guide and is not modelled.

ears.note: NOT MODELLED. The guide's Chapter 3 mounts the switch with the accessory-kit brackets and shows them in isometric drawings of a different switch ("Illustrations in this chapter depict the mounting of a DCS-7050QX-32S switch") that carry no measure. The data sheet lists the spares KIT-7101, KIT-2POST-1U-NT, KIT-7101-RK, KIT-7101-LD-RK and KIT-GND-EXT-1RU. No figure measures a bracket position, and the kit guides are not held, so no ear position is written and no rail kit is listed in chassis.kits. Recorded in the gap rack-ears.

environment.note: Guide Table 2: operating 0 to 40 C, storage -25 to 70 C, altitude 0 to 3,000 m, humidity 5 to 90 percent non-condensing. Data sheet: operating 0 to 40 C, storage -40 to 70 C, humidity 5 to 95 percent, altitude 0 to 3,000 m. Storage temperature and humidity differ: gap `environment`, the guide's used.

front-legend.note: The model legend reads "7280SR3-40YC6" under the maker's wordmark at the top left (read at 847 px; the print is small). THE WORDMARK IS NOT DRAWN: a logo-zone region is reserved over it and the plain model text is set. The text is as the guide's caption names the model.

front-ports.note: Figure C-7 at 1.882 px/mm. Forty SFP cages in two stacked rows (ports 1 to 40), twenty columns in ten two-column blocks: the tab centres of ports 1, 3, 5, 7 read 18.3, 32.6, 52.8 and 67.0 mm, ports 35, 37 and 39 read 309.2, 329.4 and 343.9, a column pitch of 14.25 (the registry's ganged-SFP pitch, whose cages abut) inside a block and 6.0 mm more between blocks. Six QSFP100 cages in two stacked rows of three columns (41 to 46), centred 366.9, 392.7 and 417.7 mm, a pitch of 25.4 (the cages are drawn in a wider bezel than the registry's 18.5 mm opening). The rows read from the tabs at 18.0 and 32.2 mm down, a row pitch of 14.2. The belly-to-belly orientation is the library's convention (upper cage upright, lower turned 180); the figure is too small to show the latch side.

fru-bays.note: Guide Appendix E (E.2 power supplies, E.3 fan modules) gives removal and installation procedures, and the data sheet calls the supplies "1+1 hot-swappable" and the fans "hot-swap". SO THE TWO POWER SUPPLIES AND THE TWO FAN MODULES ARE BAYS. Nothing on this chassis is a built-in unit. The management block, the USB port and the console port are part of the chassis and are placements.

gate-1-front.note: Figure C-7 passes. The raster is 847 x 235 pixels (125 ppi, the sharpest front figure of the guide); the body measures about 828 px wide and 82 px tall (aspect 10.1), against the data sheet's 440.0 / 43.7 = 10.07, so the figure is near-orthographic and carries geometry at 1.882 px/mm (the 440 mm body is the scale anchor, its left edge read at 2 px and its top at 87 px). One pixel is 0.53 mm, so every position is good to about 0.6 mm, and every one is `estimated` because it is read off a picture and no dimension states it. The cages were read from the white port-number tabs in a six-times enlargement.

gate-1-rear.note: Figure D-1 is a 553 x 141 px raster whose chassis is 551 px between its edges and 54 px tall (aspect 10.2 against 10.07), 1.252 px/mm over the 440 mm body; positions are good to about 0.8 mm. The guide draws the rear generically (D-1 to D-4) and does not say which model uses which. The 7280SR3-40YC6 is mapped to D-1 by its two fan modules (data sheet: "Hot-swappable Fans 2 (N+1 redundant)"), its 1RU height, its two power supplies and its management ports at the rear (Figure C-7 has none at the front). THE MAPPING IS ESTIMATED.

interface-names.note: Not printed and not modelled. EOS names ports Ethernet1 to Ethernet46 and Management1; this is the vendor's convention and no held document prints it.

lifecycle.note: Searched 2026-10-23 (web searches of Arista's end-of-sale notices) for a notice for the 7280SR3-40YC6 and 7280SR3E-40YC6-M: none found. The notices the searches returned were for older 7280 models and for the 7280SR3K-48YC8 (notice 23789) and 7280CR3K-36S (notice 23790) series, not for this one.

other-faces.note: No source draws the top, bottom or sides flat. The guide's installation figures are isometric. Each carries an `empty` sentence. The 1RU grounding point is on the bottom of the chassis (guide section 4.2, Table 5, KIT-GND-EXT-1RU); no figure measures it.

port-lamps.note: Guide Appendix A.1.2, Table 10: off link down, green link up, yellow software disabled, flashing yellow failed diagnostics. Figure C-7 draws a green diamond at the outer edge of each SFP block row, left of the left cage and right of the right one, 21.5 mm down in the upper row and 28.2 mm down in the lower: one lamp a SFP port is modelled, the left lamp for the left column and the right lamp for the right. The QSFP cages carry a column of three or four green dots at the cage's left edge that are not modelled (gap `qsfp-lamps`).

port-numbering.note: Figure C-7 (callout 7, "Port numbers") prints 1 over 2, 3 over 4, and so on, 1 to 40 across the SFP columns and 41 over 42 to 45 over 46 across the QSFP columns. The odd number is the upper cage. The figure prints each number twice: on a white tab over the cage opening, and small with an up or down triangle in a row above the cages. A seated cage hides the tab, so the model prints the numerals in the band between the two rows, the odd number left of its column centre and the even one right of it. EOS interface names are not printed on the metal and are not modelled.

power.note: Guide Table 4: typical / maximum 130 W / 214 W for the 7280SR3-40YC6 and the 7280SR3E-40YC6-M, each with PWR-511-AC or PWR-511-DC. The data sheet states the same figures with typical "measured at 25C ambient with 50% load on all ports".

rear.note: Figure D-1 at 1.252 px/mm, the rear seen from behind with x = 0 at the left of the drawing. PS1 is the left and PS2 the right (callouts 1 and 6). Each power supply module is 73.5 mm wide (the data sheet's "73.5MM") at 4.4 and 361.5 mm across and 1.85 mm down. The management block is a grey plate 82.5 to 100.5 mm across with the Ethernet management port, the USB port and the RJ-45 console port stacked in it, in the order the library draws other Arista management stacks. Two fan modules 78.6 mm wide at 105.7 and 276.6 mm across and 2.55 mm down. Between the fans is a grey plate printed with ASSY NUMBER, SERIAL NUMBER and MAC ADDRESS fields and, under them, PS1 and PS2 legends beside airflow arrows (the arrows are not drawn).

rear-fan.note: Data sheet: "Hot-swappable Fans 2 (N+1 redundant)", "Fan Tray FAN-7011M" and the spares FAN-7011M-F (front-to-rear) and FAN-7011M-R (rear-to-front). Guide section 2.1: a red handle is an air-exit module and a blue handle an air-inlet one, and every module must have the same direction. The two fan modules are bays that accept FAN-7011M-F or -R; the -R configurations seat the blue modules.

sources.note: 7280R3 Series Quick Start Guide, Arista Networks, document DOC-07041-01, 63 pages, PDF created 2025-05-16 (https://www.arista.com/assets/data/pdf/qsg/qsg-books/QS_7280R3.pdf): Table 1 (dimensions and weights), Table 2 (operating and storage), Table 3 (power input), Table 4 (power draw and supported supplies), section 2.1 (airflow orientation, handle colour), Table 5 (grounding), section 4.5 (serial and management cables), Appendix A (status indicators, Tables 9 to 13), Appendix C (Figure C-7, the front panel of the DCS-7280SR3-40YC6 and 7280SR3E-40YC6-M), Appendix D (Figure D-1, the rear panel with two fan modules), Appendix E (field replacement). 7280R3 Series Data Center Switch Router Data Sheet, Arista Networks, 03-0045-59, dated August 11th, 2025 (https://www.arista.com/assets/data/pdf/Datasheets/7280R3-Data-Sheet.pdf): the model comparison of the 7280SR3-40YC6 and 7280SR3E-40YC6-M, the power supply specifications and the ordering information. The 2022 7280 1RU Gen 3 guide (https://www.arista.com/assets/data/pdf/qsg/qsg-books/QS_7280_1RU_Gen3.pdf) does not list this model, so Figure C-7 has no second reading. Held and checked first: intake COVERAGE.md and SOURCES.md, which list no photograph, Visio stencil, 3D model or CAD file for this model (Arista publishes none; the stencil zip could not be fetched). The data sheet's picture of the face is a thumbnail. No drawing, photograph or logo is copied into the library, only transcribed facts and new drawings.

speed-strips.note: Guide Figure C-7: a cyan strip under each two-column SFP block row, a lavender strip under each QSFP row, a cyan "25G" tag at the lower left and a lavender "100G" tag at the lower right. The strips and the two tags are drawn in those colours and spelled as read. A small dark hole sits at the left of the first block (4.7 mm across, 21.5 mm down), and two brass-coloured screw heads sit on the bottom lip at 146.2 and 284.8 mm.

status-lamps.note: Guide Appendix A.1.1, Table 9 and Figure C-7 callouts 3 to 6: a system status lamp (blinking green on power-up, green normal, blue locator, amber for two or more failed fans), a fan status lamp (green, amber for one module removed or failed, red for two or more) and a status lamp for each of the two power supplies (green operating, off removed or faulty). Four lamps in a column at 432.9 mm, 7.6, 10.9, 14.5 and 17.8 mm down, with a symbol or legend right of each: a circled mark, a fan, and PS1 and PS2.

vents.note: The figure shows a perforated grid along the top (0.8 to 9.6 mm down, 27.5 to 427.5 mm across) and a row of slits along the bottom lip (40.9 to 43.0 mm down). Each is drawn in its measured extent; the individual squares are not drawn one by one.

Table 9 - PSU Status: green PSU functioning and fully operational; off PSU removed or not operating properly
